inspiration: Overlay pipeline: one plain textured-quad shader (world times projection, one sampler, per-vertex colour) draws the whole overlay. Recreate the same minimal shape for our HUD with our own shader and art.

Placeholder-first art: a loud fallback texture stands in for any missing image, so gaps are obvious during development. Our version could be a high-contrast check in our own colours, drawn only when a load fails.

Text as its own layer: glyph wrapper and layout class are separate from draw calls, so the HUD can measure and wrap text before drawing. Reference Chorizite.Core/Render/TextLayout.cs and Chorizite.Core/Render/ACFont.cs.

Panels described as data: the framework leans on HTML/CSS-style panel descriptions instead of hand-built widgets. Our version could let artists restyle HUD panels from a layout file without code changes.
One icon for two places: the launcher icon and the repo logo are the same PNG (identical hash). Keep one brand image and reuse it, rather than a second copy.
Honest scope: the repo holds no creatures, items, armour, zones or effects. Its creative value for us is UI and rendering plumbing only.

briefs.label: Missing-art checker tile
briefs.why: A loud placeholder that cannot be mistaken for real art; it makes missing textures obvious in development.
briefs.keep: High-contrast two-colour check; fixed size; shown only when a texture fails to load.
briefs.change: Our own colour pair, not the file's; a broken-frame glyph in the corner; a slow pulse so it is noticed.

briefs.label: Single-pass HUD quad shader
briefs.why: One small shader for every overlay element keeps the HUD cheap to draw.
briefs.keep: One vertex stage (world times projection); one texture sampler; per-vertex colour.
briefs.change: Add an atlas UV rectangle per element; add a palette lookup for tinting; add a soft-edge mask for panel borders.

briefs.label: Measure-then-draw text module
briefs.why: Separating measure, wrap and draw keeps HUD text crisp and lets labels size themselves.
briefs.keep: Layout is data, separate from drawing; wrapping happens before any draw call.
briefs.change: Our own bitmap face; different wrap rules for chat versus world labels; signed-distance glyphs for scaling.
